invocation: W=$(mktemp -d) || exit 9; cp -R "$1"/. "$W"/ || exit 9; cd "$W" || exit 9; bash ./setup.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 9; CPP="${2%/*}"; CPP="${CPP%/*}"; ARGS=""; [ -f args.txt ] && ARGS=$(cat args.txt); FLOW_GATE_CPP_DIR="" CM_RECEIPT_HELPER="$CPP/scripts/counter-model-receipt.py" bash "$2" $ARGS; rc=$?; rm -rf "$W"; exit $rc
limits: WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES: that scripts/flow-finish-gate.sh refuses a PASS verdict when no counter-model review is recorded for the branch at a commit reachable from HEAD, and accepts one when a receipt or a committed skip reason is. WHAT IT DOES NOT: that the review was any good, or that it covered the final diff - the match is by ANCESTRY, so a review taken earlier on this branch satisfies a later commit. That weakening is deliberate and is documented on verdict() in the gate; whether a review covered the final diff belongs to #1082. THE KNOWN-BAD IS THE INTEGRATION REMOVED, NOT A MALFORMED RECEIPT. A control over counter-model-receipt.py alone still passes with the whole integration torn out, which is the vacuity #1171 exists to end reproduced one level up; tests/test_counter_model_review.py already covers receipt shape and is not what this measures. The anchor is therefore the gate's own pre-#1171 decision - pass without asking - and it is INERT on all three bad cases. EVERY CASE RUNS ON THE FALLBACK LANE (FLOW_GATE_CPP_DIR=""), so the cases stay fast and hermetic and none of them depends on uv or a CPP checkout being present; the enrolment evaluation is lane-independent, sitting above both verdict lanes. CM_RECEIPT_HELPER IS INJECTED because the stable path ~/.claude/scripts/counter-model-receipt.py is a SYMLINK into the primary checkout: a case run from a worktree would otherwise score the primary checkout's helper rather than the one under test, and would have scored a copy with no `skip-reasons` verb at all while this issue was being built. THE check-summary CASE IS A GOOD CASE ABOUT A NEGATIVE: it carries the worst receipt state in the control and must still pass, because /flow:check produces no PR and so has nothing to enrol. It guards the scoping, not the check. NOT COVERED HERE, deliberately: the main-side squash-merge hazard. After a squash merge the branch commits never land and --is-ancestor answers NO for all of them, so a main-side copy of this check would red every merged PR. That is pinned as an executed fact in tests/test_flow_finish_gate.py rather than as a case, because the correct verdict there depends on WHERE the gate runs, and a control case cannot carry that context. STATUS IS CHECKED POSITIVELY: the bad-receipt-with-unusable-status case pins that a receipt matching this branch and commit but carrying a status that is neither `ran` nor `skipped` reports UNKNOWN and reds, rather than being accepted because it merely is not `skipped` - the defect the counter-model review of this change found in its first cut. THE ALLOWLIST IS ADDRESSED WITH `--`: bad-skip-reason-shaped-like-a-grep-option pins that a reason of `-ecodex-absent` is refused. Without the terminator grep read it as the option `-e codex-absent` and matched, so a reason outside the committed set passed the check that exists to close exactly that door (counter-model review pass 2).

anchors.why: CONSTRUCTED: there is no released gate that asked this question badly - before #1171 the gate did not ask it at all, so no historical sha can serve as the anchor. It reproduces the real pre-#1171 decision: reach a pass verdict without consulting enrolment.
